about: Phase 6 statement-level audit of the Lean physics volumes (docs/research/CLAIM_TIGHTENING_ROADMAP.md). One row per physics-sounding theorem/lemma in lean_proofs/Vol*.lean, decided from the Phase 6 review (lean_proofs/check_statement_audit.py --review) and the module inventory in PROOF_AUDIT.md. Rows may carry a `previous_name` -- a name this pass retired; the gate checks that the retired name is a declaration nowhere and a live token nowhere.
method: Rows are judgements recorded per declaration, not machine-proved claims: a witness is checked to exist (and to differ from its theorem), a stated_condition to occur verbatim in the statement, a source to exist, and a previous_name to be absent from the corpus with comments masked. What the kernel can check is checked by CI's lake build ToE, which compiles every witness and source named here. `previous_name` is validated on any row, not only on `renamed` rows: a rename performed by a later pass lands under the new name and keeps its disposition.

dispositions.witness: the statement is about a declared, non-degenerate object or instance (named in `witness`); its hypotheses, where it has any, are realized
dispositions.conditional: the statement carries its hypotheses in its own signature (`stated_condition` quotes the text)
dispositions.renamed: the name was changed so it no longer overstates; `previous_name` is the retired name and must not survive anywhere
dispositions.carried: true only from data the model carries (structure field, postulate, placeholder or constant definition, definitional restatement, or degenerate instance), so no non-degenerate witness exists; `source` names the declaration that carries it

lexicon: The candidate census is lexical: a theorem/lemma counts when one of the words in its name (split on _, ., camelCase) is a PHYSICS_TOKENS word in check_statement_audit.py. The lexicon is a floor, not a ceiling.
